name: Home SOC lab - measured coverage
description: Measured ATT&CK coverage of a self-built three-VM home SOC lab (Windows 11 endpoint with Sysmon and advanced audit policy, Wazuh 4.14.7 all-in-one, Kali attacker). Scores come from queries against the alert index, not from mapping tables: 0 = nothing exercised and no mapped telemetry; 1 = the mapped telemetry exists only partially or only as an adjacent mechanism, and detection is untested; 2 = telemetry generated and collected, and nothing actionable matched it - either no rule at all, or only a catch-all that treats the activity like background noise (a measured detection gap); 3 = a rule fired on this technique's own activity in this lab. Collection for score-2 entries is inferred from the agent configuration, not observed, because the manager indexes only what matched a rule. Only techniques with measured evidence appear. Note that TA0005 is named Stealth in ATT&CK v18. Full matrix and caveats: detections/coverage-matrix.md.

techniques.comment: Telemetry configured and verified on the endpoint: PowerShell 4104 ScriptBlockLogging and 4103 ModuleLogging, Security 4688 with command line enabled by registry, Sysmon EID 1 with CommandLine, ParentCommandLine and hashes. Detection evidenced through the sub-techniques below.

2026-08-08: powershell.exe -EncodedCommand raised Wazuh rule 92057 at level 12 - on a Sysmon Event ID 1, NOT on the PowerShell 4104 the exercise had predicted, although the 4104 was generated. Own Sigma rule drafted (proc_creation_win_encoded_powershell.yml), not yet deployed. Evidence: investigations/001-first-alert-triage.md.

2026-08-11: the powershell -> cmd transition fired rule 92004 at level 4 - the only alert produced by 11 Sysmon EID 1 events in the window, and it fired on the ancestry pattern rather than on process creation. Evidence: investigations/002-process-telemetry-correlation.md.

2026-08-08: rule 60109 level 8 on 4720/4722, rule 60110 level 8 on 4738 x2, rule 60111 level 8 on 4726. Three single-event rules; nothing correlates them into the one sequence they belong to (user created, added to Administrators and deleted inside 8 seconds). Evidence: investigations/001-first-alert-triage.md.

2026-08-08: a test service install alerted through Event ID 7045 from the System channel, while Event ID 4697 from the Security channel reached the SIEM and produced 0 alert documents. Detection depends entirely on one of the two available sources. Evidence: investigations/001-first-alert-triage.md.

Never simulated; studied 2026-07-31 (4 mitigations, of which M1026 removing local admin eliminates it). The UAC linked-token mechanism it abuses was measured directly: 4 of 4 remote invocations produced a 4624 pair - 8 x 4624 and 4 x 4672 in all, elevatedToken %%1842 with a 4672 and %%1843 without - and launched processes carried TokenElevationType %%1938 (Limited). No bypass path exercised and no rule.

2026-09-07: correlation rule 60204 'Multiple Windows Logon Failures' fired twice at level 10 by accumulating 20 rule-60122 events (level 5) inside a short window. Evidence: investigations/003-smb-rdp-attack-chain.md.

2026-09-07: 18 attempts from 10.10.10.5 - 15 x 4625 with SubStatus 0xC0000064 (non-existent accounts), then 3 x 0xC000006A (real account, wrong password). The guessing never succeeded; the successful 4624 that follows came from a known-valid credential supplied deliberately, to generate post-authentication telemetry. Alerts fired, but rule 60204 does not read SubStatus, so enumeration and targeted guessing are indistinguishable to it. Failures were spaced about 2 s apart by EnableAuthRateLimiter (2000 ms), which is the mitigation's fingerprint, not the attacker's.

2026-08-08: ipconfig /all and systeminfo produced only generic level-3 4688 alerts from catch-all rule 67027. Telemetry generated and collected; no rule reads the command line for discovery utilities.

2026-08-11: whoami.exe produced a Security 4688 matched by catch-all rule 67027 at level 3 - byte for byte the same treatment as sppsvc.exe - and no Sysmon rule fired on it. A single discovery command is indistinguishable from background noise; it has to be detected as a sequence. Evidence: investigations/002-process-telemetry-correlation.md.

2026-08-08: nmap -sS -p- covered 65,535 ports in 88 s (8 open, 65,527 filtered) and produced 0 attributable alerts. 2026-09-07: an -sn sweep plus -sS -sV against 7 ports left 2 Sysmon EID 3 events and 0 Security 5156, because the Filtering Platform Connection subcategory is deliberately not audited - and enabled it would only have recorded the 8 permitted connections. The subcategory that records a dropped packet is Audit Filtering Platform Packet Drop (5152/5153); it is off in this lab and was never measured. Structural collection gap with the subcategories this endpoint enables: needs a network sensor, not a rule.

2026-08-11: Security 4798/4799 (enumeration of a user's local group membership, the SharpHound signature) generated 2 events and produced 0 alerts, confirmed against a widened time window. The 2026-08-08 batch (net user, net localgroup administrators) produced only level-3 4688 alerts.

2026-09-07: the SMB null session preceding share enumeration produced Security 4624 ANONYMOUS LOGON, type 3, NTLM, from 10.10.10.5, flagged by rule 92652 at level 6 - the only reliable trace of the whole reconnaissance phase, and a level 6 in an exercise whose twelve level-15 alerts were all noise. The alert fired on the logon that carried the enumeration, not on the enumeration: the authenticated --shares listing of ADMIN$/C$/IPC$ left no distinct event, because Audit Object Access -> File Share (5140/5145) is deliberately off in this lab.

2026-09-07: rule 92657 fired 3 times at level 6 with this mapping. With NLA active the 4 failed RDP logons appeared as 4625 logon type 3, not type 10; only the completed graphical session produced 4624 type 10 (Negotiate, User32) with TS-LocalSessionManager 41->42->21->22->24. A detection keyed on 'type 10' would miss every failure against a default-configured target.

2026-09-07: the guessing phase failed, so a known-valid local credential was supplied deliberately to generate the post-authentication telemetry. It was accepted over SMB (4624 type 3, NTLM, rule 92657) and later over RDP (4624 type 10). The account is a local administrator, so access to ADMIN$ and C$ implies full control of the endpoint. Nothing in the alert itself separates this from a legitimate administrator logon.

Studied 2026-07-31 and never executed. Two mitigations: M1041 (encrypt traffic end to end) eliminates the technique outright and leaves nothing to detect. The channels its detection strategy needs - Sysmon 11, then Sysmon 1 with the browser as parent, then Sysmon 3 - are ingested by this lab, but no event for the technique exists.

Rule 92213 ('Executable file dropped in folder commonly used by malware', level 15) carries this mapping and fired 18 times - 1 on 2026-08-08, 5 on 2026-08-11, 12 on 2026-09-07 - and every one was a false positive on __PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1 written by the signed system powershell.exe. No tool transfer was ever staged, so what exists is the adjacent file-create mechanism, not the technique. Scored 1 rather than 3: a rule that has only ever fired on something else has not detected this. Tuning debt; the replacement rule is drafted and not deployed.
2026-08-08: co-mapped with T1098 on rule 60111 (level 8) firing on Security 4726, the deletion of the test account created eight seconds earlier.

Not simulated; identified by negative evidence on 2026-08-11. Sysmon EID 1 carries OriginalFileName (PowerShell.EXE), which survives a rename and is collected here; Security 4688 has no equivalent field, so the technique is undetectable from the Windows Security log alone. No rule reads the field.

Not simulated, but its mapped telemetry was measured on 2026-08-08: Security 4697 was confirmed in the endpoint log with Get-WinEvent, the Security channel is forwarded by the agent, and a wazuh-alerts-* query returned 0 documents containing 4697. ATT&CK lists zero mitigations for this technique, which makes it a detection problem by definition.

Numbered T1070.001 before the ATT&CK v18 regrouping under T1685; the old ID no longer places on a v18 matrix. Security Event ID 1102 has never been generated in this lab and no query has ever been run against it, so its detection path is untested - the gap is the missing exercise, not an empty query result. Planned; the base-limpia snapshot exists for the rollback.

2026-08-08: rule 60154 ('Administrators Group Changed') fired at level 12 on Security 4732 and again on 4733, inside a create-user / add-to-Administrators / delete sequence completed in 8 seconds. The ATT&CK mapping is Wazuh's own, attached to the rule; 4732 arguably belongs to T1098.

Theory only, studied 2026-07-31. Not reproducible in this lab: there is no mail server. Three mitigations, two of which (SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks and user training) depend on parties the defender does not control. Numbered T1672 before the ATT&CK v18 regrouping under T1684.

legendItems.label: 0 - Not covered: never exercised, and no mapped telemetry exists in this lab
1 - Telemetry only partial or adjacent, detection untested - includes techniques whose mapped rule has only ever fired on something else
2 - Generated and collected, nothing actionable matched: either no rule fired, or only a level-3 catch-all that treats the activity as background noise
3 - A rule fired on this technique's own activity in this lab (see comment for the rule ID and date)

metadata.name: Lab
metadata.value: Self-built 3-VM home lab: Windows 11 Pro endpoint (Sysmon, advanced audit policy) -> Wazuh 4.14.7 all-in-one on Ubuntu Server 24.04.4, Kali attacker, VirtualBox NAT network 10.10.10.0/24

metadata.name: Scope
metadata.value: 23 techniques with measured evidence. Techniques this lab has not touched are absent rather than scored 0.

metadata.name: How scores were obtained
metadata.value: Endpoint side with Get-WinEvent; SIEM side with JSON queries against wazuh-alerts-* through the Wazuh dashboard console proxy, filtered on data.win.system.systemTime rather than @timestamp (the manager clock ran about 1.8 s behind the endpoint).

metadata.name: Honest coverage
metadata.value: 12 of 23 techniques (52%) had a rule fire on their own activity. T1105 is excluded from that count and scored 1: its mapped rule fired 18 times and all 18 were false positives on an adjacent PowerShell temp file. Only 3 firings came from a rule reading a pattern rather than a single event. Rules written by the author: 21 Sigma documents across 12 files, all drafted, none deployed to the manager - so techniques detected by a rule of the author's own: 0.

metadata.name: Largest uncovered tactic
metadata.value: Stealth (TA0005, called Defense Evasion before ATT&CK v18): 4 of 5 techniques uncovered, 5 of 6 if T1548.002 is counted here as well as under Privilege Escalation. Discovery is level with it at 4 of 5, and three of those four gaps (T1016, T1033, T1087) are rule gaps: the activity ran, the telemetry was generated and forwarded, and only a catch-all matched. The fourth, T1046, is an architecture gap that needs a network sensor, not a rule.

metadata.name: Caveat
metadata.value: A coverage claim built by searching an alert index is bounded by the ruleset, not by what the endpoint produced: on 2026-08-08 about 2,100 events reported to the manager left 835 alerts indexed; on 2026-08-11, 172 events generated produced 36 alerts (a first, window-clipped pass reported 167 and 27).
